pages.text: Tomorrow was Mom's birthday. Pipo took out the coins he had saved.
"I will choose her a gift at market." Holding his coin purse tightly, he went there.
The three grown-ups were already at the market. "A gift? We will help!"
Grandpa chose a walking stick and put it in Pipo's arms. "Since olden days, nothing beats a walking stick as a gift."
Mrs. Goose put a big hat on him. "Everyone at market talks about this hat!" Mr. Horse added the biggest radish. "Why waste time choosing? Quickly, the biggest one!"
Pipo's arms were full of stick, hat, and radish. He could not see ahead.
Pipo quietly put everything down. "I want to choose Mom's gift myself."
He slowly looked around the shops. Sparkle—a little bell like the lamb's caught his eye.
He paid his coins and bought the bell. Jingle, jingle, a clear sound.
Mom attached it to her hat. Jingle, jingle. "Now I will always know where Mom is!" The three grown-ups swapped the walking stick, hat, and radish among themselves.
